mainEntity.name: What is the standard order of a board meeting agenda?

acceptedAnswer.text: Call to order, roll call and quorum, approval of the agenda, approval of prior minutes, consent agenda, reports, old business, new business, executive session if needed, announcements and adjournment. Bylaws can change this order. Many boards also move key decisions earlier, so directors discuss them while they are fresh.

mainEntity.name: Who sets the board meeting agenda?

acceptedAnswer.text: The board chair sets the agenda, usually with the CEO or executive director and the board secretary. Directors can request items through the chair. Committee chairs submit their reports in advance, and the final version goes out with the packet so every director sees one identical plan.

mainEntity.name: How far in advance should a board agenda be sent?

acceptedAnswer.text: Send the agenda and board packet 5 to 7 days before the meeting so directors can read reports and prepare questions. Quarterly board with long financial packs? 7 days is safer. Ask directors to send questions in advance, so meeting time goes to decisions rather than clarifications.

mainEntity.name: Is an agenda required for a board meeting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many bylaws and some state laws require notice of meetings, and special meetings often require stating the purpose in advance. Even when not required, an agenda is standard good practice. Check your bylaws for notice rules, especially for special meetings and votes on major decisions.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between old business and new business?

acceptedAnswer.text: Old business covers items carried over from previous meetings; new business covers matters raised for the first time. Gradually, old business should shrink. Same item 3 meetings in a row without a decision? Give it a deadline or a smaller working group.

In executive session, the board meets privately, often without staff, to discuss confidential matters such as CEO performance, legal issues or personnel. Any formal action is usually taken back in open session.
